entities.summary: Cleon was an Athenian politician and general (strategos) during the Peloponnesian War. He was born into a wealthy tanner family, and his father, Cleaenetus, was a prominent Athenian citizen. Cleon's rise to power was swift, and he became one of the first prominent Athenian politicians of the 5th century BC to obtain power from outside the established elite. As a young man, Cleon served in the Athenian army, fighting in several battles against the Persians and the Spartans. He quickly gained a reputation for his bravery and strategic thinking, and he became a leader among the Athenian hoplites. Cleon's most notable achievement was his role in the Athenian victory at the Battle of Amphipolis, where he led a successful campaign against the Spartans. This victory cemented Cleon's reputation as a brilliant military strategist and solidified his position as a key figure in Athenian politics. Despite his many achievements, Cleon's life was cut short when he was assassinated in 421 BCE. His legacy lived on, however, and he remains one of the most important figures in Athenian history.
